1_prompt_stability.answer: PARTIAL -- individual prompt-vs-prompt rank correlation is modest (135M mean Spearman rho=0.364, 360M mean rho=0.466; both well short of 1.0), but a SMALL SET of layers (135M: 19, 27; 360M: 30, 23) are overwhelmingly more sensitive than the rest in nearly every prompt.

2_category_stability.answer: YES, strongly -- category-vs-global Spearman rho ranges 0.55-0.87 (135M) and 0.61-0.93 (360M), and the top-5 most sensitive layers per category overlap heavily across all 11 categories (layers 19/27 in 135M appear in every single category top-5).

3_model_stability.answer: PARTIAL -- exact-layer-index overlap after normalized-depth mapping is modest (top10_overlap_after_depth_mapping=0.40), but both models concentrate their most-sensitive layers in the mid-to-late depth region (quintiles 2-4 of 5) and each model has ONE standout near-final-layer that dominates sensitivity (135M layer 27 at depth 0.93; 360M layer 30 at depth 0.97).

4_context_stability.answer: YES, fairly strongly -- on the same 5 prompts, ctx=2048 vs ctx=8192 rankings correlate at Spearman rho=0.71, Kendall tau=0.51, top-10 overlap=80%, with the top-2 layers identical and in the same order at both context sizes. Caveat: these short prompts consumed similar actual token counts at both ctx settings -- this tests KV-cache-capacity effects, not long-context-usage effects specifically.

5_policy_usefulness.answer: YES, clearly on rel_l2 -- a ranking built ONLY from 21 train prompts beat EVERY naive layout (early/late/alternating/random) on logit_rel_l2 at EVERY intermediate Q8-budget tested (4/8/12/15/20/24 layers), evaluated on 10 held-out prompts never seen during ranking construction. Mixed but still favorable on top1_preservation (5/6 budgets) and delta_nll (wins at higher budgets, random sometimes better at low budgets).

unstable_task_dependent_evidence.note: Beyond the 2-3 dominant layers per model, the remaining ~27-29 layers show much lower and more prompt-dependent support (see category_rankings.json support_by_layer for the full distribution) -- consistent with modest prompt-vs-prompt rank correlation on the FULL ranking even though the TOP few layers are highly stable.

memory_pressure_finding: At the real GTX 1650 ctx=180000/360M boundary, all 4 layer-selection strategies for an 8-of-32 Q8 budget cost identical memory and all achieve full residency -- confirming sensitivity-based selection is a zero-memory-cost choice at this real hardware boundary (quality-at-boundary itself not measured, by design, to avoid real OOM risk).

decision_gate_inputs.cross_prompt_stability: weak-to-modest for the full ranking, strong for the top 2-3 layers
decision_gate_inputs.cross_model_stability: modest at exact-index level, moderate at depth-region level
decision_gate_inputs.cross_context_stability: strong (with the important actual-token-count caveat disclosed)
decision_gate_inputs.holdout_policy_beats_naive: yes, consistently on rel_l2; mostly yes on top1; mixed on delta_nll
